svg.title: How the Uqda network works
svg.desc: Every device that installs Uqda becomes a node. The nodes connect to each other and carry each other's traffic, encrypted. Together, they are the network.
svg.text: UQDA · عُقدة · A NETWORK MADE OF NODES
Every device that installs Uqda becomes a node. The nodes connect to each
other and carry each other's traffic, encrypted. Together, they are the network.
Uqda means node. Install it on anything, and that device joins the network as an equal.
A key pair made on the device.
A few nearby nodes: on your
for others when it lies on the
Your address is calculated from your key. Without the key, nobody can use it.
A connection that arrives from 200:1a2b:3c4d::7 really comes from the holder of that key.
Programs can use the address as a login, with no passwords.
Your programs see ordinary IPv6. Uqda does the rest, layer by layer.
Browser, SSH, games, chat, your own service
Plain IPv6: 200::/7 addresses, nothing to learn
Replies pass; new connections only if a rule allows them
End to end, forward secrecy, optional group secret
Spanning tree, greedy forwarding, bloom-filter lookups
TCP, TLS, QUIC, WebSocket; every link proves its key
Peers: how nodes find each other
A peer is a direct link between two nodes. A node needs only a few.
Every link starts with a handshake. Each side proves it holds its key over a fresh random
value, so a recorded handshake cannot be replayed to impersonate a node.
Nobody plans the map. The nodes agree on one by talking to their neighbours.
Coordinates = the path from the root. No node knows the whole network.
A node keeps a few records
How a packet finds its way
Three simple rules, applied by every node, route traffic across the world.

bloom filter of the keys behind
it, so lookups go the right way.
Each node hands the packet to
Shortcuts are used when they exist.
When a link breaks, the sender
is told, looks the target up
What anyone in the middle sees
Traffic is encrypted end to end. Nodes in the middle carry it but cannot open it.
that traffic passes, its size and timing
read it, change it, or replay it
Forward secrecy: old traffic stays protected even if a key leaks later. TLS or QUIC on a link
also hides the protocol from your internet provider.
Everyone shares the same roads. One setting decides who may talk to you.

private: open only what you share.

For your devices, family or team.
A packet's journey, step by step
From one app on your laptop to an app on your friend's computer.
A program sends to your friend's 200:… address, like any IPv6 address.
The operating system routes all of 200::/7 to the uqda0 interface.
The address points to a key; a lookup follows bloom filters to it.
Session keys from X25519, ratcheted; the group secret is mixed in.
Each node forwards it to the peer closest to the target.
Only your friend's node can open it. Replays and outsiders are dropped.
Rules decide. The app sees a normal connection from your address.
The firewall decides what comes in
On by default for new nodes. Rules match a key, address, subnet, protocol and port.
Reply to a connection you opened
From nothing to a private network of your own devices.
• A one-time code, also as a QR
$ sudo uqda join uqda-invite-1:… # new device
Anything that listens on IPv6 already works. The sender's address is a login you can trust.
Your peers see your IP address.
